title: Jest kawa · nie ma kawy
title_en: There is, there was, there will be
note:
C1 Block 1, unit 1 — the level opens on the cheapest high-value unit it has, exactly as B2 opened on b2_copular_future. ZERO NEW LEMMAS and teaches_lemmas is deliberately empty (the b2_copular_future / b2_passive / adj_gen convention): jest/są since a1_hello, był/była/było/były since a2_past_byc, będzie/będą since a2_bedzie, nie ma since a1_negation, and every Genitive used here since a1_gen_endings, a2_gen_pl and b2_gen_pl_full.

PAYS TWO EXPLICIT FENCES, both logged by their own packs. b2_copular_future: 'the plain EXISTENTIAL future (Będzie kawa) is fenced… it is the twin of the negative above and they are not worth separating.' And its sibling, the negated future nie będzie kawy, which the same note deferred to b2_neg_gen — which then taught the Genitive of negation off a transitive verb and never moved nie ma out of the present at all. Both twins land here together, which is why they are worth one unit and not two.

THE ONE FACT, and it is an asymmetry rather than a paradigm: the POSITIVE existential has an ordinary Nominative subject, so być agrees with it in all four shapes (Był chleb / Była kawa / Było mleko / Były gazety) exactly as it does in Tata był w domu; the NEGATIVE existential has NO SUBJECT AT ALL, so there is nothing to agree with — it is one frozen form in each tense (nie ma / nie było / nie będzie) whatever the gender and however many there are, with the thing behind it in the Genitive. Slide 4 puts the two columns side by side because the contrast IS the content.

ANCHORS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. The fronted place phrase is amply precedented and was checked rather than trusted: W szkole były dzieci (a2_family2), W parku były grzyby (a2_nature2), W lodówce jest mleko (a2_house), W sklepie nie ma gazet (a2_gen_pl), W sklepie nie ma mleka i nie ma chleba (b2_neg_gen). So neither the inversion nor the Genitive plural after nie ma is new here — a2_gen_pl already shipped the plural negative, which is why the plural rows in this unit read as recognition of something owned rather than as a second system.

HOMOGRAPH CATCH THAT CHANGED THE UNIT: książki is TAUGHT ONLY AS A GENITIVE SINGULAR (a1_gen_ki [39], a1_negation [40]) and is NOT owned as a nominative plural, so the natural English 'there were books' cannot be built and appears nowhere. gazety (a2_plural_nom [55]) is the plural used throughout instead, in precisely the job that pack taught it in, with gazet (a2_gen_pl [58]) as its Genitive. This is the AGENTS homograph rule doing real work: the auditor would have passed Były książki without a murmur.

DISTRACTORS are taught words in the wrong slot, never fabricated non-words (the b1_imperative_rule convention): Był kawa / Było kawa / Nie była kawy / Nie są gazety are ungrammatical strings built only of pool-legal forms, and each is explained rather than left to sting. Two quiz items discriminate by TENSE alone (all four choices grammatical, one right) so the board is not only about agreement.

FENCED, deliberately: no plural adjectives anywhere (Block 2 has not happened — the standing C1 fence on -ych/-ym/-ymi); no counted subjects (W domu było pięć okien is held by b2_num_subject and b2_plural_gym for c1_word_order); no na + Accusative (na obiad drafted and cut — c1_przez/c1_na_acc own that governor); książki in any slot; and no cukru/soku/samochodu, all verified NEW by b2_neg_gen and still absent.

PISANIE: eleven items, every one a minimal pattern unit of two or three words with no bolted-on part, so all are typed whole under the James 2026-08-06 cap and its refinement — the b1_wrapup 'Planuję spotkanie.' precedent. No composed sentence is typed anywhere; nothing here belongs in the repair queue.

intro.title: A frame you have had since A1 — never yet moved out of the present
intro.title_pl: Jest kawa. · Była kawa. · Będzie kawa.
intro.body: You have been saying Jest kawa since the first weeks, and Nie ma kawy almost as long. Neither sentence has ever been put into the past or the future. Both go there with verbs you already conjugate — but the two halves behave differently, and that difference is this unit.
intro.body_pl: Jest kawa. → Była kawa. → Będzie kawa.

intro.title: The positive half agrees — the thing is an ordinary subject
intro.title_pl: Był chleb. · Była kawa. · Było mleko. · Były gazety.
intro.body: In the positive sentence the thing is a subject in the Nominative, and być agrees with it exactly as it does in Tata był w domu. Four shapes in the past, because that is how many the past of być has. In the future there are only two, because będzie and będą are all the future has.

examples.en: There were newspapers in the shop.
There will be soup at home.

intro.title: The negative half has no subject at all
intro.title_pl: Nie ma · nie było · nie będzie
intro.body: Nie ma never changed for you in the present, and this is why: there is nothing in the sentence for it to agree with. The thing is not the subject — it is in the Genitive, behind the verb. The past and the future work the same way, one frozen form each, whatever the gender and however many there are.

intro.title: One frame, two behaviours
intro.body: Side by side the asymmetry is the whole unit. The positive sentence has a subject, so the verb has four shapes to choose between. The negative sentence has none, so it has one. Turning a positive existential negative therefore does two things at once: it freezes the verb and it moves the thing into the Genitive.

examples.en: There is no milk in the fridge.

quiz.explain: kawa is the subject of this sentence and it is feminine, so być agrees with it — the same była as in Mama była w domu.

Two things at once. There is no subject here, so the verb cannot agree with anything and stays było; and the thing itself is in the Genitive — kawy, not kawa. Nie ma kawy is the same sentence in the present.
mleko is neuter and it is the subject, so the verb takes the neuter form. The last option is the negative of this sentence, and note what it does to the noun: mleko becomes mleka.
gazety is a plural subject and nothing in it is a person, so the verb takes były — the same form as in W parku były grzyby.
The future has only two shapes, będzie for one thing and będą for more than one. gazety is more than one, so będą.

The negative existential is nie ma in the present whether the thing is one or many — the plural changes only the Genitive behind it, gazet. The other two are the same sentence in the past and in the future.
The positive existential leaves the thing in its plain Nominative form. Only the negative moves it into the Genitive, which is where problemu belongs.
More than one thing, and the sentence is positive, so the subject stays in the Nominative and the verb agrees with it: są.
będzie never becomes będą in a negative existential, because there is no subject to make it plural. And chleb goes into the Genitive: chleba, the one masculine in this course that does not take -u.
czas is masculine, and it makes no difference: the negative existential has nothing to agree with, so it is było here exactly as it is with a feminine kawa.
This one is positive, so the verb does agree — and gazety is plural. Będą would move it to the future.

quiz.prompt: There was no water in the shop. →
quiz.explain: Past, negative, so both halves move: było stays frozen whatever the thing is, and woda becomes wody.

type_items.explain: mleko is neuter, so the past of być takes its neuter form — the same było you already say in Było dobrze.
The verb froze and the noun moved: mleko became mleka. Both happen together every time an existential goes negative.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: There was no bread in the shop.
Type: Yesterday there was no time.
Type: There were newspapers in the office.
Type: There is no milk in the fridge.
Type: Tomorrow there will be no problem.
Type: There was a problem at work.
use_items.explain: Positive, so problem is the subject and stays in its plain form — and being masculine it takes był.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: There will be soup at home.
Type: Yesterday there was coffee, but today there is no coffee.
use_items.answer: Wczoraj była kawa, ale dzisiaj nie ma kawy.
accepts: Wczoraj była kawa, ale dzisiaj nie ma kawy.
Wczoraj była kawa, ale dzisiaj nie ma kawy
use_items.explain: The same coffee twice, in two shapes: kawa as a subject in the positive half, kawy in the Genitive after the negative.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: There was no water in the shop, but there was tea.
use_items.answer: W sklepie nie było wody, ale była herbata.
accepts: W sklepie nie było wody, ale była herbata.
W sklepie nie było wody, ale była herbata
use_items.explain: Both halves are in the past and both are about a feminine noun, yet only the second one agrees: była herbata, but nie było wody.
